facts.label: Marriage license fee
facts.quote: The cost of a marriage license is $81.00.
facts.note: The Clerk's fee schedule page (fees-payment.php) still prints $80.00 under 'Filing Fees Effective January 1, 2014'; the FAQ page and the JP 5-1 page both print $81.00.

facts.label: Civil ceremony at a Dallas County courthouse (JP 2-2, Mesquite, weekday by appointment)
facts.quote: Monday thru Friday from 10:30a-3:30p: $80 CASH ONLY - By appointment
facts.note: The same page prints '$100 CASH ONLY - Walk-in' on the next line. Fees are set court by court. Other Dallas County JP courts print different fees (see the extra facts: JP 5-1 $60, JP 3-1 $150).

facts.label: Waiting period
facts.display: 72 hours after the license is issued (a district judge can waive it)
facts.quote: After you have purchased your marriage license, state law requires 72-hours before the ceremony takes place to get married, unless you obtain a waiver from a district judge.

facts.label: How long the license is valid
facts.display: 90 days from the day it is issued
facts.quote: A marriage license expires 90 days after the date the license is issued.

facts.label: ID you bring
facts.display: Both of you: valid government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID or ID card) and your Social Security number
facts.quote: Both persons must be present and provide: Valid government-issued photo ID. Acceptable forms of ID include: Driver's license, passport, military ID, or an identification card issued by Texas or another state, the United States or a foreign government

facts.label: How to get the license / book the ceremony
facts.display: Fill in the application online first (you get an order number), then both of you go to the County Clerk's office at 500 Elm St., Suite 2100 with that number
facts.quote: Marriage license applications must be completed on-line.

facts.label: Order number needed at the Clerk's office
facts.display: Keep the order number from the online application: you need it when you come in
facts.quote: Please make note of this order number, because you will need this number for your walk-in with Dallas County.

facts.label: Both people must be there
facts.display: Both parties present to buy the license
facts.quote: Both parties will have to be present to purchase a new marriage license.

facts.label: County Clerk office address, phone and hours
facts.display: 500 Elm Street, Suite 2100, Dallas, TX 75202; (214) 653-7099; 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday
facts.quote: Records Building - 500 Elm Street, Suite 2100, Dallas, TX 75202 Phone: (214) 653-7099 | Fax: (214) 653-7176 Hours: 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., Monday - Friday

facts.label: How you can pay the license fee
facts.display: No personal checks: cash, money order, cashier's check, business check or credit/debit card

facts.label: Twogether in Texas course: cheaper license and no wait
facts.display: Takes $60 off the license fee and waives the 72-hour wait
facts.quote: Twogether in Texas reduces your marriage license fee by $60 and waives the 72-hour waiting period.

facts.label: Social Security number
facts.display: Bring your number (the card itself is not required)
facts.quote: Social Security number. You are not required to show your social security card.

facts.label: Witnesses
facts.display: Witnesses are not required; guests are welcome (JP 3-2 courtroom)
facts.quote: While witnesses are not required, you are welcome to have guests.

facts.label: Certified copy of your marriage license
Other courthouse ceremony fee: JP 3-1 (North Dallas Government Center, LBJ Freeway)

facts.label: Other courthouse ceremony fee: JP 5-1 (page still lists the old East Dallas address)
facts.display: $60 weekday 10:30a to 3:30p, cash only, appointment required
facts.quote: Monday thru Friday from 10:30a-3:30p: $60 CASH ONLY

steps: Fill in the Dallas County marriage license application online and write down the order number it gives you.
Both of you go to the County Clerk's Records Building (500 Elm St., Suite 2100) with photo ID and your Social Security numbers, and pay the $81 license fee (no personal checks).
Wait 72 hours after the license is issued before the ceremony, unless a district judge waives it or you hold a Twogether in Texas certificate.
Book a ceremony with a Dallas County Justice of the Peace court; each court sets its own fee (JP 5-1 $60, JP 2-2 $80 by appointment, JP 3-1 $150 on its pages).
Hold the ceremony within 90 days of the day the license was issued, or the license expires.
left_out: A single county-wide courthouse ceremony fee: the County Clerk does not perform ceremonies; each Justice of the Peace court prints its own fee (or none) on its own page.

JP 3-2 (Judge Seider) regular weekday ceremony fee: its page prints only '$400 ceremony fee' for holiday and holiday-weekend dates (dated July and August of an earlier year) and says other times are 'fee to be determined'.

Whether an appointment is required at the Clerk's office: the FAQ says a marriage license appointment must be scheduled, the marriage-license page speaks of a 'walk-in' with the order number, and the JP 3-1 page says no appointment is required, so no single fact is given.

A residency rule: the JP 3-2 page says 'Only Dallas County residents, based on the address shown on applicants' state issued identification', but the County Clerk's own pages do not state it (see notes).
A 'courthouse ceremony' room inside the County Clerk's Records Building: no official page states one.

notes: SOURCES AND METHOD: every quote was copied from a page downloaded with curl on 2026-10-28 (raw pages in .cache/raw/dallas/) and verify_quotes.py reports problems: 0. The web-search budget ran out part-way, so later venue, photographer and florist leads came from Zola's Dallas-area listing pages (leads only) and each business's own site was then fetched directly. Search-engine summaries were not trusted: one said Drive Up & Wed's 'Kiss & Go' was $975 for ten minutes, but its live page prints $250 for fifteen minutes; one said JP 3-1 weddings cost $100, but its page prints $150. Only curl-verified values are used. COURTHOUSE: (1) The Dallas County Clerk issues licenses; it does not marry people. Ceremonies are done by Justice of the Peace courts, and each court prints its own fee (JP 5-1 $60, JP 2-2 $80 by appointment / $100 walk-in, JP 3-1 $150), so the guide should say 'about $60 to $150, depending on the court' and name the court. (2) License fee: the FAQ page and the JP 5-1 page print $81.00; the Clerk's fee schedule page still prints 'Marriage License without Certificate $80.00' under 'Filing Fees Effective January 1, 2014'. $81 is used. (3) Residency conflict: the JP 3-2 page says 'RESIDENCY REQUIREMENTS - Only Dallas County residents, based on the address shown on applicants’ state issued identification.' for the Dallas County Clerk; the Clerk's own marriage-license, FAQ and fee pages say nothing about residency, and the same JP 3-2 page says Collin County has none. Not stated as a fact; the coordinator should phone the Clerk, (214) 653-7099, before writing 'non-residents welcome' or 'residents only'. (4) Appointment conflict: the FAQ says 'A marriage license application must be completed online and a marriage license appointment must be scheduled'; the marriage-license page talks of a 'walk-in' using the order number; the JP 3-1 page says 'No appointment is required but marriage license application must be completed online' and also says 'Dallas County now has three satellite locations to receive your marriage license! Appointments at the three satellite locations are released 30 days in advance.' (5) The Clerk's pages say 'Effective October 5th, the Vital Records Division will be open on Mondays and Fridays from 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM' with no year given; the standard hours line is 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday. (6) JP 5-1's page still lists 3443 St. Francis Avenue, which the county banner says is closed (moved to 9731 Lake June Road), so its $60 fee may be stale. JP 3-2 (Judge Seider) prints no regular weekday fee, only '$400 ceremony fee' on holiday dates from an earlier year. (7) The Dallas Parks guest limit (50 people) and chair limit come from the department's Terms and Conditions PDF (revised January 2020; saved as raw/dallas/dallasparks_condition.pdf); verify_quotes.py cannot read that URL as a PDF, so that line is stored as guest_limit_text, not as a checked quote. The $25 per hour is on the HTML page and is checked. $25 per hour with a two-hour minimum means at least $50, but the page does not print $50. VENUES: 12 entries from 8 businesses (Blush Event Garden, Skip The Courthouse, Drive Up & Wed and Heirloom Hideaway have 2 entries each) sorted by amount. Bouré Event Studio's guest count is on its FAQ page (checked quote in capacity_quote); its $600 is a room rental for a 4-hour event, Monday to Thursday, not a wedding package. Soma Winery (Fort Worth, https://www.somavino.com) was left out: its page prints 'wedding and event packages beginning at $500 and have capacity for up to 100 guests' but names no small, micro, elopement or weekday package. Penrose House's elopement price page does not give a guest number (the $6,500 tier says 'up to 50 guests'), so max_guests is null; Princeton is about 45 minutes from downtown Dallas. Heirloom Hideaway & Arboreum: the page says prices are 'effective for new bookings as of January 2026'; the $675 couple-only price is marked 'Available Monday - Thursday' on its packages overview page. Blush Event Garden has four locations (Addison, Downtown Dallas, North Plano, Lake Highlands) and says 'Holiday pricing may apply on select dates'. Other pages looked at but not used because no small-group price and guest count were printed together: Little Wren Weddings (Rockwall), Chapel at Chestnut Square (McKinney), Hotel Crescent Court, Dallas Arboretum (rates are in an Issuu guide and its ceremony pages returned 404 to curl), Azalea Weddings, Carlisle Room ($1,995 weekday, no guest count), Reflections Venue & Gardens (Plano, Mon-Thu $2,000, no guest count), Dallas Woman's Forum (Mon-Thu $1,995, seated capacity 100). Blush Event Garden's Signature elopement ($750, 2 hours, reception tables for up to 20) and Flourish Events Dallas's Sun-Thu small-ballroom micro reception ($1,000) are also on their pages but not listed. PHOTOGRAPHER: Shelly Voss (McKinney) prints $400/hour with a 1-hour minimum for courthouse ceremonies inside an estimator form; the text is in the HTML. Alternatives seen on their own sites: The Grace Pictures (Dallas/Houston) 'Courthouse Wedding / Marriage Civil begin at $500' (https://www.thegrace.pictures/dallas-houston-wedding-photographer-videographer-pricing/); The Velvet Frame (Dallas) 'COURTHOUSE ELOPEMENT, starting at $1,499 (+tax)' (https://thevelvetframe.co/micros-and-elopements-or-the-velvet-frame). FLORIST: RainFlorist Designs (Frisco) prints a range, '$125-$350 ($200 average)', so amount is null and amount_low / amount_high carry the range per the brief. Alternatives: Petite Petal (serves Dallas, McKinney, Frisco, Plano) 'Simple Toss Bouquet $50–$60' (https://www.petitepetalflowers.com/pricing); J Blooms 'Bridal bouquet $275 - $375'; Best Buds Flowers 'Brides Bouquet: $300-450+'. Etsy was not used.
